pipelineWaterfall.title: Pipeline Waterfall
pipelineWaterfall.subtitle: How your pipeline moved this period. Each bar shows how many deals changed state — created, advanced, regressed, won, lost. The net delta is the bottom-line pipeline change in dollars.
pipelineWaterfall.emptyTitle: No stage transitions in this window.
pipelineWaterfall.emptyDesc: Stage transitions are recorded automatically when you change a deal's stage. Historical deals (before this feature was added) won't appear retroactively.
pipelineWaterfall.footer: Stage transitions are recorded automatically when you change a deal's stage. Historical deals (before this feature was added) won't appear retroactively.
pipelineWaterfall.chartSubtitle: Number of deals per transition type in the selected period.
pipelineWaterfall.hintTotalTransitions: How many times deals changed stage in this period.
pipelineWaterfall.hintNetDelta: Net change in pipeline value — the sum of all Amount Δ across transitions this period.
pipelineWaterfall.hintTopMover: The transition type with the most deals this period.
pipelineWaterfall.hintAmountDelta: Change in total deal value for this transition type (won/created add, lost subtracts).
pipelineWaterfall.hintCreated: New deals that entered the pipeline.
pipelineWaterfall.hintAdvanced: Deals that moved forward to a higher-probability stage.
pipelineWaterfall.hintRegressed: Deals that stepped back to a lower-probability stage.
pipelineWaterfall.hintReopened: Deals re-entered from a closed (won/lost) stage back into the pipeline.
pipelineWaterfall.hintReassigned: Owner changed without a stage change.

dealVelocity.title: Deal Velocity
dealVelocity.subtitle: See where deals slow down and where your sales team needs support.

dealVelocity.bottleneckBannerDesc: Start with “{stage}”: slow deals can stay here for {duration}. Review those deals and assign a clear next step.
dealVelocity.emptyDesc: Once deals start moving between stages, you’ll see stage times and problem areas here.
dealVelocity.howToReadDesc: Compare the typical time with slow deals. A large gap means some customers are getting stuck and the next step should be reviewed.

dealVelocity.typicalTimeHint: Half of deals move through this quickly

dealVelocity.dealsBehindMetricHint: Deals that spent the longest time in this stage are shown first.
dealVelocity.noVisibleDealDetailsHint: The metric uses historical data, but your access permissions may hide the underlying deals.

accountEngagement.title: Account Engagement
accountEngagement.subtitle: Account-based marketing view. Each row is a target account with its current engagement score, ICP fit grade, and 30-day intent signals. Best-fit accounts that have gone quiet bubble to the top — those are the ones to re-engage first.
accountEngagement.stalePriorityTitle: {count, plural, one {# stale-priority account} other {# stale-priority accounts}}
accountEngagement.stalePriorityDesc: Best-fit ICP (tier 1/2) accounts with low engagement and no signals in the last 30 days. Marketing should re-engage these before chasing lower-fit accounts.
accountEngagement.emptyTitle: No accounts in this segment yet.
accountEngagement.emptyDesc: As marketing identifies target accounts and intent signals are captured, they will appear here.
accountEngagement.footerScore: Engagement score (0–100), based on recent activity signals.
accountEngagement.footerGrade: Grade — ICP fit letter (A best fit, F disqualified). ICP tier — strategic-ranked target list slot. Stale-priority = tier 1/2 with score < 25 and zero 30-day signals.

promote.title: Promote companies to target accounts
promote.desc: Pick companies from your CRM to track as ABM target accounts. Their fit grade is computed automatically; engagement starts at 0 until intent signals arrive.
promote.hintMore: Showing the first {count}. Use search to narrow down.

detail.whyUnassigned: This company's profile is empty — add its industry, size and revenue to get a fit grade.
detail.scoreVsGradeBody: Grade = how well the company FITS your ideal profile (firmographics). Engagement score = how ACTIVE it's been (signals). They move independently.
detail.staleExplain: Best-fit account that's gone quiet — reach out first.
detail.hotExplain: High recent engagement — strike while it's hot.
detail.tierHint: ICP tier — strategic priority slot (1 = best fit, 4 = low). Auto-derived from firmographics.
detail.gradeHint: Grade {grade} — fit with your ideal customer profile (A best … F disqualified).
detail.unassignedHint: Not graded yet — the company profile (industry / size / revenue) is empty.
detail.taskDesc: Created from Account Engagement. Reach out to {name} and move the deal forward.
detail.taskCreated: Task created — see your Tasks board.

glossary.title: What the numbers mean
glossary.grade: how well the company fits your ideal profile (size, industry, revenue).
glossary.tier: strategic priority slot; 1 is a top target, 4 is low-fit.
glossary.score: how active the account has been recently — built from intent signals, not firmographics.
glossary.stages: the ABM lifecycle: Target → Engaged → MQL → SQL → Deal → Customer.

attributionModels.title: Marketing Attribution
attributionModels.subtitle: Multi-touch attribution models split a deal's revenue across the campaigns that contributed to it. The default model recalculates each campaign's credit every time a deal advances.
attributionModels.zeroTitle: Recompute ran, but nothing was attributed.
attributionModels.zeroNoDeals: No closed-won deals were found. Attribution is computed only over won deals — close deals in a Won stage, then recompute.
attributionModels.zeroNoTouchpoints: Found {deals} won deal(s), but no touchpoints matched them. Check that:
attributionModels.zeroCheckLink: won deals have a contact or company set (ideally a campaign too);
attributionModels.zeroCheckTouchpoints: touchpoints are being recorded (campaign email sends/opens/clicks, event registrations);
attributionModels.zeroCheckBackfill: the touchpoint backfill has been run for historical data.
attributionModels.emptyDesc: Admins set up the initial models (first-touch / last-touch / linear). Campaign credit is recalculated whenever a deal advances.
attributionModels.footerTouchpoints: Touchpoints are marketing interactions (email opens, ad clicks, page views, form submits, event attendance). Each campaign's attributed revenue is recalculated on every model run.
attributionModels.footerSlices: Each campaign's influence is recalculated whenever a deal advances.

modelTypeDescs.first_touch: Full credit to the first touchpoint
modelTypeDescs.last_touch: Full credit to the last touchpoint
modelTypeDescs.u_shaped: Higher weight to first + last; rest split

attributionModels.formDescriptionPlaceholder: Optional — how and when this model is used
attributionModels.formHalfLifeHint: Recent touchpoints get exponentially more credit. 7 = a touch 7 days before the deal closes is worth half of one at close.
attributionModels.formUShapedHint: The three weights must add up to 1.0 (e.g. 0.4 / 0.2 / 0.4).
attributionModels.formCurveHint: Each point maps a journey position (0 = first touch … 1 = conversion) to a relative weight. Any positive numbers — they're normalized and interpolated across touchpoints.
attributionModels.errorCustomWeights: Each curve point needs a position in 0–1 and a weight above 0.
attributionModels.customCurveApiManaged: This model uses a multi-point custom curve created via the API. Edit it through the API — the 3-point editor can't represent it.
attributionModels.confirmDelete: Delete model “{name}”? Its influences and run history will be removed.
attributionModels.confirmArchive: Archive model “{name}”? It will no longer be recalculated.
attributionModels.errorHalfLifePositive: Half-life must be a positive number of days.
attributionModels.errorUShapedRange: Each weight must be between 0 and 1.
attributionModels.errorUShapedSum: The three weights must add up to 1.0.

entitlements.title: Customer support terms
entitlements.subtitle: Company-level support terms connect a customer to an SLA policy, support level, validity window, and ticket milestones. When a ticket is created for that company, LeadDrive can apply these deadlines automatically.
entitlements.onTrack: {count, plural, one {On track — # milestone met this week} other {On track — # milestones met this week}}
entitlements.emptyDesc: Create the first draft term for a customer company. After that, add milestone rules and activate it so new tickets receive the right SLA deadlines.
entitlements.footerOverdue: Overdue = open milestone past its due date — silent SLA breach risk. At-risk <24h = open and due within 24 hours.
entitlements.footerEachEnt: Each entitlement adds detailed milestones (first response, problem identified, workaround, resolution, escalation) on top of the SLA-policy timer.
entitlements.titleOverdue: {count, plural, one {# overdue milestone} other {# overdue milestones}}
entitlements.titleAtRisk: {count, plural, one {# milestone due soon} other {# milestones due soon}}

entitlements.formDesc: Create the customer-level shell first. Milestone rules and activation are managed in the next step of the workflow.

entitlements.missingSlaPolicies: Create an active SLA policy before adding support terms.

entitlements.editingHint: Editing {company}. Company and SLA policy stay locked for audit safety.

entitlements.permissionLifecycleDesc: Only administrators can run lifecycle actions for customer support terms.
entitlements.noFilterResults: No support terms match these filters.
entitlements.cancelReasonPrompt: Why is this support term being cancelled?

entitlements.createdNotice: Draft support term created. Continue in the highlighted card to add milestone rules.

entitlements.supportLevelAfterDraft: Next: create the draft, then apply or edit the rules inside its card.

contractLifecycle.title: Contract Lifecycle
contractLifecycle.subtitle: Two-stream view of where contracts are stalling. Upcoming and overdue renewal alerts on the left; contracts stuck pending approval (grouped by current bottleneck stage) on the right.
contractLifecycle.noRenewals: No renewal alerts in the next 90 days.
contractLifecycle.footerRenewals: Renewal alerts are scheduled 90/60/30/14/7 days before a contract expires; only pending alerts appear here.
contractLifecycle.footerApprovals: The approval queue shows each contract's next stage awaiting approval. Stages are sequential — a stage unlocks only after the previous one is approved. The age shows how long that stage has been waiting — red after 7 days.
contractLifecycle.confirmApproveDesc: This advances the approval chain. Review the contract before confirming.
contractLifecycle.confirmRejectDesc: This rejects the whole contract and stops the chain. A reason is required.
contractLifecycle.bottleneckJump: Jump to this stage in the queue

identityMergeQueue.title: Identity Merge Queue
identityMergeQueue.subtitle: Likely-duplicate profile pairs, detected automatically. Reviewers can see why each pair was flagged (similar email, phone, or name) and check it before approving.

identityMergeQueue.emptyDesc: A daily scan flags likely-duplicate profile pairs by similar email, phone, or name. Every pair here is reviewed by you before merging — pairs at {auto}%+ are marked high-confidence, {manual}–{auto}% standard. Exact-duplicate profiles (identical email or phone) are merged automatically and never appear here.

identityMergeQueue.footerCron: Profiles are rescanned daily to surface new likely-duplicate pairs.

identityMergeQueue.relMonthsAgo: {months, plural, one {# month ago} other {# months ago}}

chatbotRules.title: Chatbot auto-reply
chatbotRules.subtitle: Set up automatic replies to messages your customers send on social channels — no coding needed.
chatbotRules.guideIntro: The bot reads each incoming message and, if it matches one of your rules, replies instantly for you.
chatbotRules.guideStep1: Turn on auto-reply for your organization (the switch below).
chatbotRules.guideStep2: Create a rule: choose when it should fire and what the bot should say.
chatbotRules.guideStep3: Keep the rule “On”. Only “On” rules reply.
chatbotRules.guideStep4: Done — the bot now answers customers on the channels you picked.
chatbotRules.exampleBody: When a message contains “price, how much”, the bot replies: “Thanks! Our manager will send the price list within an hour.”
chatbotRules.masterOnTitle: Auto-reply is ON for this organization
chatbotRules.masterOffTitle: Auto-reply is OFF for this organization
chatbotRules.masterOnDesc: Rules marked “On” below will reply to matching messages.
chatbotRules.masterOffDesc: Nothing will reply until you turn this on — even rules marked “On”.
chatbotRules.channelSwitchesHint: Enable or disable each channel where the bot may send automatic replies.
chatbotRules.qualificationTitle: AI lead and marketing task creation
chatbotRules.qualificationHint: AI verifies real commercial intent with a phone number, then creates a lead and a task on the selected board.
chatbotRules.qualificationRulesHint: Created once only when a phone number is present and AI confidence is high. Due in 24 hours on weekdays or 72 hours on weekends.
chatbotRules.keywordsHint: Separate variants with commas. The bot also understands diacritics, transliteration, and small typos such as ölçü/olcu/olchu.
chatbotRules.replyPlaceholder: Type the reply the bot will send…
chatbotRules.priorityHint: If several rules match, the higher number replies first.
chatbotRules.tip1: The bot won’t reply to the same chat twice within 5 minutes — so it never spams.
chatbotRules.tip2: If no rule matches the message, it’s left for your team to answer — auto-reply never blocks a real conversation.
chatbotRules.tip3: Leave “channels” empty to reply everywhere, or pick specific ones.
chatbotRules.noRules: No rules yet — create one above.
chatbotRules.masterOffWarning: You have active rules, but auto-reply is OFF — turn on the master switch above so they can reply.

meddpicc.intro: MEDDPICC is a set of eight questions that shows what we already know about a deal and what information is missing. In each section, record the known fact, supporting evidence, and next step.
meddpicc.scoreGuide: Score meaning: 1 — no information · 2 — assumption only · 3 — partly confirmed · 4 — strong evidence · 5 — fully confirmed with the customer
meddpicc.savedNoPermission: Not saved — your role has no access to the MEDDPICC field
meddpicc.whyPlaceholder: Record the known fact: name, amount, percentage, or date...
meddpicc.nextPlaceholder: Record the next step needed to get the missing information...
meddpicc.hint_metrics: How much money, time, or capacity will the customer gain from our solution? Be specific: for example, reduce costs by AZN 5,000, grow sales by 15%, or save 2 hours per task.
meddpicc.hint_economicBuyer: Who can release the budget and approve the contract? Do we know their name and role, and have we spoken with them directly?
meddpicc.hint_decisionCriteria: What requirements will the customer use to choose a supplier? For example: price, delivery date, size, quality, integration, and security. Which three matter most?
meddpicc.hint_decisionProcess: Who influences the decision, which meetings and approvals are required, and by what date must the decision be made?
meddpicc.hint_paperProcess: Which documents and approvals are required after the customer says yes and before payment? Are legal, procurement, security, contract, and deadline known?
meddpicc.hint_identifyPain: What is blocking the customer today? How does the problem cost money, time, or customers? What happens if they do not solve it?
meddpicc.hint_champion: Who inside the customer's company wants our solution, defends it when we are absent, and shares information? What is their personal reason to help?
meddpicc.hint_competition: What is the customer comparing us with: another company, an in-house solution, the current supplier, or no change? Why are we better than each option?
